To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the NOBM method is valid for stationary phi-mixing processes and that the NOBM confidence interval is valid for stationary ergodic processes that satisfy the moment conditions.

(i) the NOBM confidence interval is valid for a stationary phi-mixing input process if the moment conditions are satisfied; and (ii) the NOBM method may achieve approximate normality at a smaller batch size than it requires to achieve approximate independence.

for a stationary phi-mixing output process the batch means method is valid for any batch size, and that the classical confidence interval method is valid for a fixed batch count and increasing batch size whenever the moment conditions are satisfied.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the asymptotic behavior, in terms of the batch size, of the NOBM method when it is applied in the analysis of stationary, phi-mixed processes.
the convergence properties of the batch means method for simulation output analysis.
the asymptotic properties of the NOBM method when applied to a stationary phi-mixing stochastic process;
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NOBM confidence interval is a valid method for estimating steady-state mean response, provided that the batch size is sufficiently large to satisfy the moment conditions.
the NOBM method is valid and useful, but only if it is used properly and only for those stochastic systems where the moment conditions are satisfied.
the NOBM method, as currently practiced, is a very good method, but not a great method, for the analysis of stationary simulation output processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NOBM method can be used to analyze the output from a stationary, phi - mixing process with a substantially greater degree of confidence than has been previously recognized.
the batch means method is an asymptotically optimal simulation output analysis method for a large class of stationary, phi-ming processes.

for the NOBM method, the classical batch means confidence interval for the steady-state mean is asymptotically valid under a variety of conditions that are weaker than independence of the batch means.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NOBM method can be applied with confidence to simulation output processes that are stationary and phi-mixing.

, in order to obtain valid confidence intervals for the mean response in a simulation output analysis, one should not rely on a fixed batch size and batch count but instead should choose these two quantities so as to achieve the desired confidence level and confidence interval coverage probability.
, in many cases, it may be possible to achieve approximate joint normality at a much smaller batch size than the one needed to achieve approximate independence.
